reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 the content (character-1) of a quotation-mark-delimited nonnumeric literal may be any character of the computer character set, so the compiler must accept every character (lowercase, special characters, the apostrophe, '*>', a period-space, a non-ASCII character) as literal content and keep it as the value; only the quotation mark itself is doubled (SR2).

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry gates on the literal's format: zero-length (Constructs.ZeroLengthLiteral2014), apostrophe delimiter (ApostropheQuotationSymbol2002), X".." (HexAlphanumericLiteral2002), N/B literals; at 85 they refuse those formats, not any content character of a quote-delimited literal
the literal length bound (160 at 85, 8191 from 2014) asked by LengthViolation; not the content rule

reader.edition-search: The content rule itself (STR_BODY ~["\n] and RepertoireViolation's Format-1 arm returning null) is edition-blind; grepped LiteralScreen.cs and CobolLiteral.cs for Edition/ConstructRegistry/dialectLevel.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: for this rule the content of a quote-delimited literal is free at every edition; what differs (apostrophe delimiter, zero length, hex format, length bound) is other rules
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness exercises non-ASCII characters and doubled/fullwidth quotes; it does not exercise ASCII special characters, the apostrophe, '*>' or '. ' inside a literal at 85 (the probe does)

probes.printed: --std 85 EXIT 0: [a~@#$%^&*()_+{}|:<>?`[]\;',./ *> !      ] / lower; 'apos' "quote" *> no comment / LEN-APOS=01 / LEN-Q=01 /   .   / é (identical at --std 2023)
probes.expected: every character is literal content (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1.2 SR1); a doubled quotation mark is one (SR2)

probes.printed: --std 85 compile-only EXIT 65: COBOL0900 zero-length literal requires COBOL-2014; COBOL0900 apostrophe-delimited literal requires COBOL-2002; COBOL0900 hexadecimal alphanumeric literal requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: 1985 delimits a nonnumeric literal by the quotation mark with at least one character-1 (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1 general format); later-edition formats refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1.2 SR1  (4.2.2.2.1.2 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: The lexer body admits every character but the delimiter and newline, and the Format 1 repertoire arm is null at every edition, so any character is content at 85. Probes with ASCII specials, apostrophe, *>, period-space and a non-ASCII letter compile and display intact at --std 85; edition gates only refuse later literal formats.

refuter.evidence: Probe r1a.cob (refute-1985-043/r1a-002, --std 85, EXIT 0): a literal continued in fixed form keeps the continued line's trailing spaces through margin R and the doubled quotes split over the continuation ('AB""CD' + '-    "EF""""G"' prints AB"CD + 36 spaces + EF""G); a literal whose first line is padded to column 72 with SEQ00001 in 73-80 keeps the two pad spaces and drops the sequence text (COBOL6688 warning only); ASCII specials '*', '-', apostrophe, two apostrophes inside quote-delimited literals display intact; the 85 apostrophe-delimited form is refused (COBOL0900, the correct class-c edition arm). A TAB inside a literal is expanded to the next tab stop at line entry, which is the documented implementor choice docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-157.md (owner decision R55: the tab is a positioning control, not a character of the literal); SR1 leaves the computer character set to the implementor, so this does not refute. Checks: 'OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1.2 SR1 ... the text is in SR1'; 'OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1.2 SR2 ... the text is in SR2'; 'OK §1985:IV.7.2.2 (7.2.2 Continuation of Lines) the text is in the clause'.
